preconditions.description: The number of cities N is between 2 and 200, and the number of roads M is between 1 and 50,000.
The costs of gold (G) and silver (S) coins are positive integers up to 10^9.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= N and 1 <= v <= N and 1 <= g <= 10**9 and 1 <= s <= 10**9 for u, v, g, s in roads)
preconditions.description: Each road connects two valid cities (1 to N) and has positive gold and silver requirements up to 10^9.

postconditions.expression: is_impossible or (min_cost == min((g * G + s * S) for g, s in feasible_thresholds))
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, the output is the minimum cost among all valid (gold, silver) pairs that connect all cities; otherwise, the output indicates impossibility.
The output indicates impossibility if and only if no pair of gold and silver amounts exists that makes the graph connected.

postconditions.expression: all(is_connected(roads, g, s) for g, s in feasible_thresholds)
postconditions.description: Every pair (g, s) considered in the minimization results in a connected graph where all cities are reachable from each other using roads with requirements <= (g, s).

postconditions.expression: not is_impossible and (min_cost == min(g * G + s * S for g, s in feasible_thresholds))
postconditions.description: The computed minimal cost is the lowest possible tugrik value derived from the cost formula G*g + S*s for any valid threshold pair.
